newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close week at year high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close week at year high.

text.p: French shares surged in afternoon trading almost one percent higher to finish at a year high.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 21.90 points or 0.98 percent at 2,255.47 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 20.5 at 2,259 from Thursday's close.
Operators cited positive trends in bonds, Wall Street and a recovery in the franc.
* U.S. funds were significant buyers, the head of equity sales at a big French brokerage said.
* Around one billion francs went through on Axa and UAP combined. Axa closed up 2.38 percent at 314.4 francs, while UAP firmed 1.45 percent at 139.8. The Axa offer for UAP opened on Thursday.

* Heavy trading in Elf, Total and Alcatel made up a further billion francs. Elf firmed 1.71 percent to 457.9 francs, Total up 1.74 percent to 421, as oils continued to climb. Elf sold 10 percent of Geophysique.
* Dior accounted for 200 million francs in volume, and closed up 1.25 percent at 731 francs.
* Virtually all activity was in blue chips. The CAC-40 index has gained 3.58 percent on the month.
* "UAP-Axa started things off," said one broker. The merger, often denied despite persistent rumours, has rekindled intense speculation in takeovers in the financial and other sectors.
* Paribas is often cited as a target for link-ups. The holding company closed up 0.03 percent at 360 francs.
* Casino and Promodes are seen as potential partners, despite denials.
* The market has climbed 19.06 percent since the start of the year, but has had to recover ground lost last year.
* "Outside of a crash on Wall Street or another attack on the franc, there are few problems on the horizon. It's a nice market and it could continue," said one operator.
* The CAC-40 index has broken out of a 2,230-40 range in which it has been trapped.
* Finance and leasing company Compagnie Bancaire firmed following an upgrade by Lehman Brothers to outperform from underperform. Bancaire was up 0.53 percent at 566 francs.
* Canal Plus ends down 2.67 percent at 1,168 on talk of a big sell order from a broker and Kleinwort Benson valuation study which sees it as sell down to the 1,000 franc level.
* Lyonnaise des Eaux firms 1.46 percent after launching buy-out offer for Elyo heating subsidiary to tidy up the group structure and focus on main businesses.
